title: Very Good But Needs Some Tweaks
body:
I primarily subscribed to this app as I wanted an ‘All in one’ Calendar/To-do List app which included Location Based Reminders, and there are very few out there which do. 

This app does have a load of great features and on the whole it is very well thought out, but is has some frustrating little niggles for me, for example there is no search function in the calendar, only in the tasks screen. When you add sub-tasks to a main task, the newest one added appears on top where I think the oldest on top would be more logical as you would normally work down a list clearing your oldest tasks first. Another option here would be to make them movable but at present you can’t do that either. 

The main problem for me though is the design of the Location Based Reminders. It is straightforward to use but it is the only version I’ve seen where you don’t have an adjustable Geofencing option to allow you to trigger the reminder a set number of meters (or more) from your destination. Instead you have to input a postcode or address and this can cause problems if you wanted alerted in a certain area but you may not have the actual address or postcode (for shopping reminders while approaching shops for example). Also GPS positioning is not always 100% accurate, so sometimes the alert does not trigger. It is also not possible to drag or reposition the pin on the map either, so it can be VERY limiting. 

For most users though, it will probably be fine but I subscribed to the pro version specifically for the features which still need perfecting.

title: Close, but no cigar...
body:
I've been using Any.do for as long as I can remember now and enjoy its combination of simplicity and effectiveness. 

Recent releases have brought with them a glitch that duplicates entries temporarily when you drag to reorder them, sometimes even changing the order of items around them which is beyond frustrating and pushing me very close to finding an alternative app. The ability to prioritise and reorder lists is paramount but Any.do isn't delivering the goods recently. Please fix this ASAP as the app is near perfect otherwise. Submitting feedback through your non-responsively design website also seems impossible which is why I've regrettably had to report this glitch here.

I'm hoping to award five stars for the next release, but in the meantime I'll try my best to persevere with this version.

UPDATE: Still abysmally buggy, often crashes, takes far too long to load, takes up a lot of space and often needs restarting when you can't drag items to re-order them. It also sets all items to one week in the future as default rather than the day you're currently on, which is a little inconvenient. Such a shame as this app used to be great and has so much potential!

title: New release entirely broken; giving up
body:
For those who have been using Any.do to keep track of their to-do lists on their own device without setting up an account, relying on constant access to "the cloud", trusting your data to third parties in unknown jurisdictions, etc. - do not install this update!!

Previously it was possible to bypass the sign-in step by selecting an item from the Any.do widget, which would then bring up the app.  A nuisance, but workable.

Now, however, the geniuses behind this thing have noticed this useful workaround, and have disabled it.

As a result, I have just lost access to my lists.  Well done, Any.do.  You win: I will stop trying to help you to improve the app, and will instead delete it permanently.

title: So far, so very, very good.
body: I've tried quite a few "to do" apps and most seem either far too complicated for their own good or far, far too basic - so much so that they're no better than Apple's Notes app. So finding Any.DO has been a revelation ... so far. The simplicity means adding tasks is a breeze, and the options for each task are, it seems, just about spot on. I love the "Moments" add-on - but it is a bit annoying to have to pay for this and some of the fairly basic functions, like customising your "repeat" notifications. My feedback would be to offer a limited-period trial after which a reasonable app fee is charged to continue - like £2.99. I do think £40 a year is a ridiculous amount for a "to do" app - no matter how good it is! I know you offer half-price discounts as an incentive, but still ... too much money for a year's sign-up in my opinion. For that reason I give it four stars - otherwise it would be a nailed-on five.

Without this functionality, you now have to switch between different screens to do the same thing. What before took one click and drag, now takes 5 or 6 clicks.

However a few things that can be improved:
- It would be great if we could launch the "moment" from Notification Center as well
- Add new task from Notification Center doesn't work .. It just takes me to the app where I have to add a new task
- When the phone is locked, I can't see my todos in the Notification Center .. They only appear when the phone is unlocked

The above are the only reasons this app gets 4 stars right now. Fix those and it will be a well deserved 5 stars!

title: Getting Things Done, right
body:
I'm pretty obsessive when it comes to GTD apps and rely on an easy to use powerful system throughout my daily work.
I have purchased and used the most popular apps on apples eco system, some better than others, but I am always on the look-out for the best system for 'me'.
This is my new go-to system all rolled into one neat package. 
Someone has sat down and put a lot of thought into this app from simplicity of the UI they have understood that someone needing to track tasks must have a straightforward intuitive way to do so. From the speak to create a task all the way through to the dragging and tilting functionality, it has all been thought through.
5* for engineering a human friendly software tool that I will use daily. I'd easily pay for this and any other versions the developer can create for Apples other devices. Great work. 
Download now if you continue to imagine that 'things' and 'omnifocus' etc are the best things for your daily work lists

title: Best Tasks App On The Market
body:
I've been putting off writing a review for nearly 4 months. Now with a lot of experience (over half a year) with Any.Do, and probably another 1-2 months trying other task apps,Any.Do is by far the best.

It's simple and minimalist yet beautiful and practical design makes remembering things easier than ever.  I'm not a busy person (13years old) so I don't have many deadlines to make, just things to do.  I'm also very disorganised, and Any.Do has helped me  organise myself too.

I think the reason it's the best is because it does what it says it does, does what it should do and always does what you want it to do, no more, no less. It's simply beautiful.

I hope you choose Any.Do
Make the most of it

Matthew (Aged 13)

title: Excellent and intuitive
body:
Clean, minimalist layout with only the info you need, coupled with a rather excellent predictive / automatic feature that learns (for example, you enter "Email Bob" and the app automatically checks your contacts and then places a link directly on that to-do item that opens Mail with Bob's address filled in).

Tried many other task management / to do list apps, and always return to this.

EDIT FOR UPDATE: As you can see above, I was a huge fan of the layout prior to the update but I'm actually really loving the new design changes. Not an improvement as such, as the previous design was lovely, but certainly on par, just different and perhaps more cohesive throughout the app now.

With regards to the app itself, everything above still stands. An absolute bargain, particularly considering the price of some if the similar apps, and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

UPDATE: With the recent release, and along with it the addition of the scheduled 'organise your todos' this already fantastic app just got even better!

In response to the complaint that you can't disable the speech feature, you can by simply not choosing that way to input and typing instead. No extra measures needed, just tap the empty text field rather than the microphone specifically.

The app worked for about 2 days and aside from the microscopic buttons, I think it is a very nice to-do list (love the way it syncs with Chrome on multiple computers (not sure what browsing data they are collecting though). 

The following is the transcript of my correspondence with any.do re. the problem:

> Hi! Thanks for the feedback, 
> 
> We are aware of this issue and are 
> fixing it for the future version of
> Any.DO.. 
> Please e-mail us back if you have 
> any other problems. 
> 
> You're awesome for using Any.DO!
> -The Any.DO Team
> 
>> Wed, Jun 12, 2013 at 10:43 AM....
>> Please describe the problem:
>> 
>> To do list screen has gone 
>> completely blank (no today, 
>> tomorrow, someday, etc). It 
>> seems to flash to life for a split 
>> second at startup but then is gone. 
>> Not affecting data linked with 
>> chrome desktop extn. Tried 
>> everything short of trashing app 
>> and re-installing (it tells me I'll 
>> lose the data if I remove from 
>> phone). Suggestions?
>> Thanks in advance.
>> 
>> Version: 1.9.1.1
>> Locale: en-GB
>> Device: iPhone
>> OSVersion: iPhone OS 6.0

Deleted & reloaded app. All data lost. 
I think I'll wait till they have the problem resolved Before I invest any more energy in the app.

title: Ok, but lacks a few things to make it useable
body:
The UI is actually quite good one you get your head around it. So many other to do apps get it wrong, but there are a couple if things that will mean I won't be using it yet. 

Shared tasks logic is flawed. If you share a task and the other person accosts it, if they mark it as complete you don't get told and it remains incomplete in your list. This killed it for me. 

Also on shared tasks, sometimes you get an icon that lets you "talk" to the other person but sometimes you don't, even if the email address you used to I vote them is in you address book with an associated phone number. 

Tags. Tags would be good to help me categorise things. I know I can use folders, but I like to use both.

body:
Yep pretty good alternative, but no where near as good as Astrid. 

My first impression of any.do was that it was better than Astrid. After a few days it soon became clear to me it was not.

My three main issues with it are:

1. Continuos crashing every time a task is marked complete
2. Buttons too small; not as user friendly as Astrid
3. Tasks going missing, especially recurring events too. 

This app just isn't reliable for me in comparison to Astrid - sorry guys 2/5. Looks beautiful but sadly doesn't do the job.

title: So, so good. Where have you been all my life?
body:
I've tried many, many productivity apps and to do lists in the past. The more minimal ones feel better to me but I'm always frustrated by the lack of features. The big boys (Things, Omnifocus, etc.) give much more flexibility but also feel clumsy and bloated. Like organising my productivity is a huge task in itself. And I always end up ignoring the majority of the features and just using a Today list and scheduled events. 

Any.DO gives me exactly the features I need and nothing else. I can see what I've got to do today and peek at what's coming up tomorrow. Items drop into my list when they need to. They're not nagging me from a distance.  

And it's beautiful. Really clean and well thought out. This isn't style over substance. This is proper UX design. Clever, clever touches at every turn. Smart auto completion of tasks, voice input, quick capture. Swiping tasks to mark as complete is lovely but even better is the little shake gesture to clear your completed items and get back to a focussed list of what's still to do. This is the first app I've seen use the shake gesture in a way that feels satisfying and not stupid. 

I keep noticing features. The companion Chrome Extension is excellent and the Gmail integration is pure genius (automatic task recognition and suggestion from your emails). 

The only thing I don't like about this app is the price. Take my money. I'd rather pay £40 for this app and the devs make a living from it than have it for free and wonder how long it'll be before the staff are acqui-hired and the app is 'sunsetted'. TAKE MY MONEY!

title: You don't know good till you've tried this
body:
I was happy with wunderlist that is till wunderlist 2 and the multiple problems signing in, syncing or even viewing my data offline. As a result I looked for an alternative and any.do was worth a shot

It's actually vastly superior to any other to so app. It has location reminders. Short drag downwards adds task. Longer drag adds a voice recognition task. Swipe left to cancel. Tasks autocomplete to most common choices. Plus categorises tasks based on priority so you are never overwhelmed with tasks far into the future until its time to address then

Plus the recent addition of any.moments is an unintrusive way to reprioritise your tasks dynamically day to day like mailbox app does with email. This app has no close competitor as a result and is accessible on pc via a chrome extension. Hopefully we'll see a web version soonish. 

Absolutely no sync or load issues so far I can thoroughly give this the highest approval. Any.do is the best because it isn't willing to rest on its strengths. I hope it continues its rise

author: QasimRehman

title: Absolutely stunning
body:
With what I can only describe as a 'stunning' UI, Any.DO has become one of, if not probably the most, used apps on my phone. This app has helped organise my life, and it feels like I haven't done a thing.

The interface is gorgeous, working well with the Apple ethos of simplicity. All my tasks are separated between Today, Tomorrow, Upcoming and Someday, and are added with the tap of a button. If I'm walking and remember something I can easily tap the microphone button and use dictation to add my task. The tasks can be further filtered through work and personal tasks or highlighted in red to show important tasks in the list.

The use of a downward swipe to add a new task is so intuitive I find myself doing it absolutely automatically. It just works. Another gesture, the side swipe, is used to cross off a task. This couples well with a shake to get rid of all the completed tasks, which are put into a very accessible folder. It does arouse a sense of pride when a banner appears along the bottom of the screen to show you've completed 20 tasks. This is also shareable with FaceBook, to show off your efficiency. 

The app integrates with contacts too, and simply by adding a name after a command, e.g., "Text Sarah" an icon will appear beside the reminder that lets you jump straight to your messages, with Sarah already selected. Again: it just works.

The app helpfully displays the number of today's tasks in a red notification bubble. Any.DO is nestled neatly on my iPhone dock so I can always see how many thing I wanted to get done today.

All in all this app is a MUST BUY. It's too good not to get, and I urge you to download it as soon as possible.

title: Brilliant
body:
I have tried a few apps that claim they make your life easier but they some how fall short. This one delivers on it's promises and whole lot more. Browser addition is perfect, it's where most of my reminders are set from. The folders are a clever way to organise your todos, but the true beauty is the ease you can switch from folder priority to date priority (and vice versa).

The google tasks tie up is cool, and the contacts connection is pure class. But, Location based todos are icing on the cake. 

 Apps like this should be judged on how easy it is to input data; they don't get much easier than this one (and I haven't even mentioned voice input that it has) 

 The program is slick, intuitive and very fast. Its where I need it to be, when I need it to be and telling me what I need to know.

title: Almost complete task ecosystem
body:
This app gets a lot of plaudits based on its looks, but equally important are the additional touches and functionality that others lack. 

For Gmail/Chrome users, installing the extension gets you access to your tasks and adds an excellent option to received emails so you can add a task immediately if something needs followed up at a later date.

Only reason this isn't 5 star is lack of repeating tasks, and no way to set a default alarm time (new tasks are set to the time they are being added rather than, say, tomorrow at 9am as a starting point).

author: ursul_polar

body:
Best interface I've ever seen for a to do app. I've had an iPhone for 2 years and despite having installed the 'best' to do apps, I've never found myself coming back to use one until now.

Any.DO has a wealth of features considering it's free!

- Clear user interface
- Responsive actions
- Recognises things: type 'Go to' and a list of common sentences appear such as 'to bank', 'to town' etc. Also the names of contacts: 'Text Ni..' and below comes up with 'Text Nicola Cousin'. When the app reminds you to do it, you can call / email / text from a command within the app which takes you to the relevant screen.
- Voice recognition. Not as amazing as Siri but once you know what it does understand, it's easy.
- Can add subcategories to your tasks via a 'notes' function
- View by Date order or Folder (category) order.

These are just some of the things that I love about this app and which has stood out to me, making me want to actually have things to organise!

Would like the ability to drag to reposition to the order of my folders though. That's the only discrepancy I can think of so far. Good app!!!

title: I don't usually write reviews... But...
body:
Simply put, this is an excellent programme. Nice looking interface. Easy to use and way better than the native reminders on the iPhone. The only criticism would be that it's difficult to read the Notes section (which scrolls)... Why not leave this as a text block as that's far easier and quicker to read? 

  Also, perhaps a couple of levels of priority would be nice. I.e. instead of just making the text red to indicate priority tasks (which works fine) another colour could indicate, say, Priority 2 tasks. Even better would be Numbered tasks....so that when tasks are moved about they have a "1." to "x." to the left as an ordered list.

  These are NOT criticisms though... The developers have done a really nice job.
